"I've been part of the MVP-program since the beginning, and it has been an interesting journey to follow EPiServer's growth from a small Swedish company to become a global player in Optimizely. I have a passion to understand how things work inside and then also share this with others. It's been fun teaching so many developers about this technology over the years in User Group Meetups and during Class Room training all around the world."

- Fredrik Haglund, Strategist for Kodmentor

"I'm thrilled to be in the OMVP program. It's truly an honor to be part of a group with such great, fun, and pleasant people that are characterized by how they constantly share their knowledge and inspire others. I believe the community of developers and users is the greatest asset to the Optimizely product portfolio - and the powertrain behind that is the OMVPs."

- Allan Thraen, Developer for CodeArt

"Does it sound boring working with the same CMS for 15 years? Well, it hasn't been. Websites have gone from 1024x768 optimization to responsive. Back-end has gone from WebForms to MVC to .NET 5+. Front-end has gone from simple HTML/CSS to full-fledged client-side apps with advanced JS frameworks with TypeScript, SASS, etc. Some websites are headful, others headless. Some do content, others do e-commerce. So, the CMS development has been changing constantly - but many of the great people in the community around it remain the same. I'm still talking about Optimizely products with fellow developers that I've known for many, many years now. That in and of itself is a reason for me to stay an OMVP for another 15 years."

- Ted Nyberg, Strategist for ted&gustaf

"I have been in the MVP program for many years now and it has been a continual source of inspiration and excellence amongst my fellow Optimizely developers. It’s a place you can collect, discuss, and help shape the future of the product and with the relationships we have with the Optimizely team it allows us to really help make the platform the best it can be. I have also made many friends that I’ve had the pleasure of seeing at a number of Optimizely meetups to share a beer and talk about the platform which has made us a real community. If you’re passionate about the platform it’s the best place to be without a doubt and the best part, we get to help everyone using Optimizely to make the best products for our clients."

- Scott Reed, Solutions Architect for Niteco

"Benefits of being an OMVP? How about access to an amazing brain trust made up of the nicest group of people, a true voice in the direction of the product, early previews of upcoming surprises, and did I mention the swag?!"

- Kenny Gutierrez, IT Web Developer Manager at Century Communities Inc.
